patches.old: It is typically defined by a specific income threshold (e.g., the international poverty line of $2.15 per day).
patches.new: It is typically defined by a specific income threshold. The World Bank's **international poverty line** — the line for extreme poverty — is currently **$3.00 per person per day**, measured in 2021 purchasing-power-parity dollars; it replaced the older $2.15 line (2017 PPP) in June 2025. Two higher lines are used for richer country groups: $4.20 a day for lower-middle-income countries and $8.30 for upper-middle-income countries. The line is revised periodically as price data are updated, so treat any specific figure as the current value of a moving threshold rather than a constant.

sources.title: World Bank, “June 2025 Update to Global Poverty Lines” — the international poverty line is now $3.00 per person per day in 2021 PPPs, replacing $2.15

visual.title: Three axes, and what they do to health
visual.alt: Three cards for class as the economic dimension, status as prestige and party as organised power, with three cases where they diverge and the label status inconsistency; a plotted mortality gradient falling steadily from the lowest to the highest employment grade in the Whitehall data, with a note on absolute and relative poverty; and a panel of the material, psychosocial, behavioural, access and exposure pathways alongside economic, cultural and social capital and habitus.
visual.caption: The Whitehall gradient runs the whole length of the hierarchy, which is why relative position matters and not only absolute deprivation.
